rows.ts_quote: $10.0 billion senior unsecured revolving credit facility

rows.ca_value: Amendment No. 2 and Consent dated March 14, 2025 to the Amended and Restated Credit Agreement dated March 18, 2022 (as amended by Amendment No. 1, March 17, 2023). It is a single multi-borrower revolving credit facility with Revolving Credit Loans (Section 2.01(a)), a Swingline sub-facility (Section 2.18) and Letters of Credit (Section 2.15), for the same eight Borrowers. No term loan or tranches.
rows.ca_quote: Reference is made to the Amended and Restated Credit Agreement dated as of March 18, 2022

rows.explanation: Both documents describe an amendment, extension and upsize of the existing multi-borrower revolving facility rather than a new facility. The structure is the same: a single revolver with swingline and LC sub-facilities, and the same eight Borrowers.

rows.ts_value: Maturity Date March 16, 2030, extended one year from the existing maturity of March 16, 2029.
rows.ts_quote: March 16, 2030
rows.ts_location: PDF p.1, 'Maturity Date' row (and narrative: 'currently scheduled to mature on March 16, 2029')
rows.ca_value: Commitment Termination Date is March 16, 2030 (blackline changes March 17, 2028 to March 16, 2030; Recital B describes it as a one-year extension to March 16, 2030). If that day is not a Domestic Business Day, the date becomes the immediately preceding Domestic Business Day; the amendment changed this from 'next'. March 16, 2030 is a Saturday, so commitments actually terminate on Friday, March 15, 2030. Under Section 2.05, loans to Borrowers other than the Company also mature on their 'Borrower Maturity Date' (first anniversary of the borrowing) unless the borrowing is designated long-term.
rows.ca_quote: for each Lender, March 1716, 20282030, as such date may be extended from time to time with respect to such Lender pursuant to Section 2.01(b) or, if such day is not a Domestic Business Day, the nextimmediately preceding Domestic Business Day
rows.ca_location: Section 1.01 'Commitment Termination Date', PDF p.46; Recital B, PDF p.1; Section 2.05 and 'Borrower Maturity Date', PDF pp.45, 63
rows.explanation: The stated date, March 16, 2030, is the same in both documents. However, it falls on a Saturday, and the CA's newly inserted 'immediately preceding Domestic Business Day' convention moves actual termination to Friday, March 15, 2030. That is one day earlier than the TS date (under the old 'next' convention it would have been Monday, March 18). The TS does not mention the 364-day Borrower Maturity Date for subsidiary-borrower loans. The blackline base date is March 17, 2028, not the March 16, 2029 existing maturity in the TS. This is consistent rather than a conflict: the 2029 date came from a per-Lender extension under Section 2.01(b), which does not change the definition text, and Recital B confirms a one-year extension to March 16, 2030.

rows.ts_value: Two 1-year extension options, refreshed (shown in bold as a new/changed term). No term-out option.
rows.ts_quote: Two 1-year extension options (refresh)
rows.ca_value: Section 2.01(b): any time after the Second Amendment Effective Date (changed from 'First'), the Company may request up to two one-year extensions. Each Lender decides in its sole discretion. Lenders holding at least 51% of Commitments must agree; non-extending Lenders keep their original date and may be replaced. After an extension the maturity may be no later than five years from that extension's effective date. No term-out option.
rows.ca_quote: propose to extend the Existing Commitment Termination Date for an additional one year period measured from the Existing Commitment Termination Date; provided that in no event may the Company request more than two extensions
rows.ca_location: Section 2.01(b)(i)-(ii), PDF p.61
rows.explanation: Two one-year extensions are available in both documents. The 'refresh' comes from restarting the request window at the Second Amendment Effective Date. The cap on two extensions does not expressly exclude the extension used in 2024, but the natural reading is that it counts only requests made in the new window. The 51% consent threshold, per-lender election and five-year cap appear only in the CA.

rows.ca_value: Adjusted Term SOFR is Term SOFR plus a SOFR Adjustment of 0.10% per annum, for 1, 3 or 6-month Interest Periods. Adjusted Term SOFR has a 0% Floor. The alternate rate is the Base Rate: the highest of Prime, Fed Funds + 0.50%, and 1-month Adjusted Term SOFR + 1%. Amendment No. 2 raised the Base Rate floor from 0% to 1% (blackline 'than 01%').

The CA also contains floors the TS does not mention: 0% on Adjusted Term SOFR, and a Base Rate floor raised from 0% to 1% by this amendment. The TS does not show the floor increase as a changed term. Its practical effect is very small, because the Base Rate's SOFR + 1% limb already floors it at 1% whenever SOFR is available.

rows.ca_value: No amortization. Revolving loans are repaid at the earlier of the Commitment Termination Date and the Borrower Maturity Date (first anniversary of borrowing for non-Company Borrowers unless designated long-term). document_notes:
TS: a one-page lender presentation slide, not a formal term sheet. It is the "Executive Summary - Transaction Summary" page (deck page 14, PDF page 1). It describes a one-year extension and $1.0bn upsize of Duke Energy's existing $9.0bn Senior Unsecured Master Credit Facility to $10.0bn, with the existing maturity given as March 16, 2029. It carries no date and points to a separate "Summary of Terms", which was not provided. Both slide tables (Borrower Sublimits and Pricing Grid) are misaligned in the -layout text extraction. PDF page rendering is not available here (pdftoppm not installed), so their values were confirmed with xpdf pdftotext -table and -raw output (printed to stdout, no files written). Every sublimit, fee, all-in margin and borrower-tier mapping matched the first pass. Text quotes for these tables are the cleanest contiguous fragments in the -layout file. TS terms outside group A are not reconciled here: Arrangers, use of proceeds (general corporate purposes), and the financial covenant (Max Consolidated Debt/Capitalization 65.0%, or 70.0% for DUK and Piedmont), which belongs to the covenant group. CA: Amendment No. 2 and Consent dated March 14, 2025 (SEC Exhibit 10.1) to the Amended and Restated Credit Agreement dated March 18, 2022, which was previously amended by Amendment No. 1 dated March 17, 2023. Wells Fargo is Administrative Agent and Swingline Lender. Exhibit A is a conformed blackline, and its operative terms were reconciled as amended. Exhibit B replaces Schedule 1.01(a), the Commitment Schedule (27 Lenders totalling $10,000,000,000). LIMITATIONS: (1) The text file shows deleted (struck) and inserted (double-underlined) text side by side, old value first, e.g. "March 1716, 20282030" = March 16, 2030. The new Initial Sublimits total exactly $10.0bn and the cover changes $9bn to $10bn, which confirms the old-then-new order. The first pass reports confirming struck text from strike-through line objects in the PDF content stream: Base Rate floor 0% -> 1%; maturity March 17, 2028 -> March 16, 2030; per-Issuing Lender cap $40,000,000 -> $33,333,333; all ESG/Sustainability provisions deleted. This review could not repeat that check. Indirect evidence supports the ESG deletion: the TOC has no Section 2.20, and Section 7.05 has 'theirits' edits. (2) The blackline base maturity (March 17, 2028) differs from the TS existing maturity (March 16, 2029). This is consistent: the 2029 date came from a per-Lender extension under Section 2.01(b), and Recital B confirms the one-year extension to March 16, 2030. (3) The conformed copy leaves out the signature pages, Schedule 1.01(b) (Pricing Schedule), Schedule 1.01(c) and the Exhibits. The Applicable Margin, Facility Fee Rate and initial ratings-based pricing levels therefore cannot be checked against the CA. (4) Upfront fees sit in the fee letters dated February 20, 2025, which were not provided. Corrections made in this review: two page references (Section 3.02 is p.78; Section 2.11(a) is p.65), removal of an unsupported 'standby' LC description, an added note that the named Issuing Lenders' combined fronting caps (about $400m) sit below the $800m LC sublimit, and corrected TS table-source notes.

TS: a single, undated slide headed 'Executive Summary / Transaction Summary' (deck page 14, marked CONFIDENTIAL; 1 PDF page). corrections.was: Events of Default are Borrower-specific, with no cross-default between Borrowers.
corrections.now: Events of Default are tested Borrower by Borrower, but DEC, DEP and DEF are Material Subsidiaries of the Company by definition. That creates a one-way upstream cross-default to DUK: their Material Debt payment default, cross-acceleration, insolvency or a judgment over $150m is also a Company Event of Default. Other Borrowers are linked only where one meets the 15% total-assets Material Subsidiary test for another. Added the 'Material Subsidiary' definition (PDF p.54) to ca_location.
corrections.evidence: CA PDF p.54: ""Material Subsidiary" means at any time, (i) with respect to the Company, Duke Energy Progress, Duke Energy Carolinas and Duke Energy Florida". Sections 6.01(e)-(h) and (j), PDF pp.85-86, each reach 'such Borrower or any of its Material Subsidiaries'.

corrections.was: Increased costs and capital: payable 15 days after demand, with a 90-day lookback. ... Under 8.06 the Company may replace or terminate a Lender that suspends SOFR lending, claims compensation, declines to extend, becomes a Defaulting Lender, loses Investment Grade Status, or is a Non-Consenting Lender.
corrections.now: The 90-day lookback applies only to increased costs under 8.03(a). Capital and liquidity claims under 8.03(b) have no lookback: only periods starting at least 30 days after the Lender's notice can be claimed. The Non-Consenting Lender trigger in 8.06 supports replacement only (8.06(a)). The termination option (8.06(b)) applies only while the Borrowers have Investment Grade Status and needs 3 U.S. Government Securities Business Days' notice.
corrections.evidence: CA PDF p.95, 8.03(a): "no such amount shall be payable with respect to any period commencing more than 90 days prior to the date such Lender first notifies the Borrowers"; 8.03(b): "no such amount shall be payable with respect to any period commencing less than 30 days after the date such Lender first notifies the Borrowers". PDF p.99, 8.06: "(vi) for purposes of (a) below only, any Lender becomes a Non-Consenting Lender" and "(b) if at the time Investment Grade Status exists as to the Borrowers, the Company may elect to terminate this Agreement as to such Lender".
